title: kate-text: tell an opening bracket from a closer
summary: is_opener is true for an opening bracket. A closer and a quote are false. The test goes in the existing brackets tests module.

lane.reason: A local Qwen3.8 coder model with 27B parameters on the owner Mac codes this packet. The change is one file and stays under about 60 lines.

definitions.definition:
#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
pub fn is_opener(ch: char) -> bool

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: brackets.rs has one test module named tests. Add the new test function at the end of that module, before its closing brace. Do not write a second mod tests. Add is_opener next to is_bracket. The attribute is cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code)). The body is PAIRS.iter().any(|(open, _)| *open == ch). Do not nest an if inside an if. Do not touch PAIRS, is_bracket, bracket_mate, matching_bracket, pair_of, scan, or bracket_at. The existing tests is_bracket_names_a_pair and bracket_mate_names_the_other_side stay green. Do not rewrite their assertions. The test calls super::is_opener. A left parenthesis is true. A left angle bracket is true. A right parenthesis is false. A right angle bracket is false. A double quote is false. The letter a is false. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip. Keep the change under about 60 lines. Run the full test module named in the commands, not only the new test.

regression_tests.name: brackets::tests::is_opener_names_only_the_open_side
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because is_opener does not exist. After the change a left parenthesis and a left angle bracket are true. A right parenthesis, a right angle bracket, a double quote, and the letter a are false.
